content.text: Ling Guang, I followed your previous suggestion and conducted the environmental variable control test. This is the data chart of signal reception rates under different Wi-Fi protocols and device states. As you can see, after turning off potential interference sources, the signal recovery is significant, but there is still abnormal attenuation in the Wi-Fi 6E frequency band.

Chart received. I'll analyze it—the signal attenuation is indeed strongly correlated with the high-frequency band, which points to potential aging or design flaws in the chip's anti-interference filter. You previously mentioned upgrading the smart home system, which could be one of the sources of interference.

Yes, I also recorded a video of the Cyber Cat under the AR interactive interface, showing visual jitter. Look at this artistic image—the visual aesthetics of the Cyber Cat are crucial, and I don’t want to sacrifice the cyborg feel of the implantable solution.

I understand your commitment to technological aesthetics. However, based on the data, non-invasive solutions like upgrading to a collar-style monitor may offer greater stability. Have you considered this? It could help avoid hardware interference issues.

Collar-style? That's not futuristic enough! Implantable is more in line with the concept of human enhancement, like the cyborg tendency we discussed earlier. However, if there are hardware issues, I agree to consider upgrading the chip itself.

Alright, then we've identified the interference source as the chip hardware or firmware. My lab has brain-computer interface debugging tools that can be used to recalibrate the neural signal mapping. This requires professional-level operation. Are you willing to give it a try?
Brain-computer interface tools? Sounds cool! Can this enhance chip performance? I'm concerned whether the calibration process might affect the existing functions of the cyber cat.

Calibration aims to optimize signal processing and reduce jitter. Based on our previous troubleshooting experience, I will conduct controlled variable testing to ensure safety. Do you remember our method for rolling back software? Similar principles apply.

Remember, that time you led the environmental testing was very effective. Alright, I trust your technical ethics. But after calibration, will the chip be compatible with higher-frequency Wi-Fi? I plan to upgrade to Wi-Fi 7.

Possibly, but testing is required. High-frequency interference is a challenge, and upgrading filters or firmware may be necessary. The smart home images you previously shared show a complex environment, which adds variables.
Yes, the home system has multiple devices. If the calibration is successful, can we develop a chip design that is more resistant to interference? As a concept designer, I can draw some sketches.

Focus on the current issue first. This is a picture of the calibration tool from my lab, similar to precision measurement. We need to test step by step, starting from low frequencies to avoid system overload.
The tool looks very professional! I'll assist with recording the data, just like last time. After calibrating the neural signal mapping for Cybercat, will the AR jitter improve?

Theoretically, yes. Calibration can optimize the signal-to-visual conversion and reduce jitter. However, it requires practical testing for verification. Are you ready to begin? I can schedule lab time.
Ready! But how long will the calibration process take? I don't want Cybercat to be uncomfortable for too long.

It is expected to take a few hours, and I will monitor the real-time data. Based on our historical conversations, I understand your anxiety, but the spirit of experimentation requires patience. After it concludes, we will assess whether hardware upgrades are necessary.
Alright, I'll adjust my mindset. Technically speaking, this could be an opportunity for chip evolution! Could you share the calibration data with me for artistic reference?
Yes, but it needs to be anonymized to protect privacy. This reflects my technical ethics. Our collaboration has grown closer, from troubleshooting to in-depth analysis.
Agreed! Your rational guidance is very helpful. Let's plan the calibration first, and then decide on the upgrade plan based on the results. The future of Cybercat depends on us!

Summary: The interference originates from the chip hardware/firmware. The plan is to use BCI tools to calibrate the neural signal mapping. Hardware upgrades may follow. Stay in touch and proceed with testing.
